What happens on a single collision
Priority the game uses at each collision. It checks behaviours top to bottom and applies the first one the projectile still has available. Only one line is used per collision.
Projectile checks whether it can still Split
It splits into auto-targeting projectiles and the collision is consumed
Highest priority; a projectile can only Split once
If Split is exhausted, it checks Pierce
Passes through the target and keeps its original trajectory
Counts as a hit; does not change direction or speed; uses one Pierce count
If neither Split nor Pierce applies here, it checks Fork
Splits into two projectiles at 60 and -60 degrees from the path
Only one fork unless Awakened Fork Support; a piercing hit does not fork
If still nothing applied, it checks Chain
Redirects to another enemy within about 6 metres
Applied last among enemy-targeting behaviours; same enemy not hit twice in one Chain
If nothing else applies, or at end of travel
The projectile heads back toward its origin
Lowest priority; normally once; allows one extra hit on already-hit targets

This priority is the global rule in Path of Exile 2. Specific skills or unique items can override part of it (for example forcing Fork before Pierce), so never assume a single skill's special case is the universal order.
Which behaviours can combine, and how. 'Per collision' means on a single hit; several behaviours can still appear across the projectile's whole journey.
Mutually exclusive per collision. A piercing projectile does not fork on that hit; Fork only happens once Pierce is used up (or never, if it pierces all targets).
Fork consumes the collision. After forked projectiles travel out, they may chain from terrain; enemy-chain follows only once their travel ends.
Forked projectiles can Return toward the origin at the end of their travel.
Once the chain ends, Return can trigger and bring the projectile back.
Split has top priority and can be followed by the rest in sequence across the projectile's full path.
Shotgun prevention still applies: when several projectiles are created at once, only one may collide with the same target, so extra copies can pass through without hitting.

Enemy-target Chain and terrain/object Chain are separate systems with different rules. Do not conflate them.

Only one behaviour per collision. If it pierces or forks, the enemy-chain is skipped.
Redirects to another enemy within about 6 metres; the same enemy is not targeted twice in one Chain.

Does NOT chain from terrain either

Five enemies in a row; projectile has Pierce and Chain

The projectile Pierces through the line first (Pierce beats Chain). After Pierce is used up with no more enemies in the way, it may chain from terrain or simply end. Chain from enemies does not trigger while it can still Pierce.

On hitting the enemy with no Pierce/Fork left, the projectile can chain off the wall to a second enemy. Terrain chain happens at most once by default and its chance is additive.

With no other target nearby, Fork and Chain find nothing to redirect to and travel off. Return can add one extra collision against the boss (the only already-hit target), making Return the most useful of the four here.
